step_section.name: Determining transaction price
step_section.instructions:
The ‘transaction price’ is the amount of consideration to which an entity expects to be entitled in exchange for transferring goods or services to a customer, excluding the amount collected on behalf of third parties - e.g. some sales taxes. To determine this amount, an entity considers multiple factors. 
An entity estimates the transaction price at contract inception, including any variable consideration, and updates the estimate each reporting period for any changes in circumstances. When determining the transaction price, an entity assumes that the goods or services will be transferred to the customer based on the terms of the existing contract, and does not take into consideration the possibility of a contract being cancelled, renewed, or modified.
Transaction price includes:
i. Variable consideration (and the constraint): The Company estimated the amount of variable consideration to which it expects to be entitled, giving consideration to the risk of revenue reversal in making an estimate. 
ii. Non-cash consideration: Non-cash consideration is measured at fair value, if it can be reasonably estimated, if not, an entity uses the stand-alone selling price of the good or service that was promised in exchange for noncash consideration. 
iii. Significant financing component: For contracts with a significant financing component, an entity adjusts the promised amount of consideration to reflect the time value of money. 
iv. Consideration payable to the customer: An entity needs to determine whether consideration payable to a customer represents a reduction of the transaction price, a payment for a distinct goods or services or a combination of the two.

section.name: If the previous questions were answered 'Yes' please describe the facts and circumstances and specify why the criteria mentioned above are met:
section.instruction:
As per Para 10-32-6 of ASC 606 consideration can vary because of discounts, rebates, refunds, credits, price concessions, incentives, performance bonuses, penalties, or other similar items. Hence Service credits, ARC/RRC, productivity guarantee shall be considered as variable consideration.
Please describe the approach to estimate the variable amount for each variable consideration (most likely amount, expected value) and explain why the method used better predicts the consideration to which the Company will be entitled:

questions.question: Service Credits
questions.expected_analysis: The expected value is the sum of probability-weighted amounts in a range of possible consideration amounts.

questions.question: ARC/RRC
questions.expected_analysis: The Most-likely amount is an appropriate estimate of the amount of variable consideration as the contract has only two possible outcomes.

questions.question: Productivity guarantee
questions.expected_analysis: The Most-likely amount is an appropriate estimate of the amount of variable consideration as the contract has only two possible outcomes.

questions.question: Please explain the reasonableness whether it is highly probable that a significant reversal in the amount of cumulative revenue recognized will not occur (ASC 606-10-32-11. (Please consider the likelihood and the magnitude of a revenue reversal)
questions.expected_analysis:
Since the variable considerations are measured monthly and a monthly provision for credit to be passed to the Customer for failure to meet achieve agreed service level is made by the service delivery team which is reviewed and approved by BU Finance Head of respective vertical. Based on the approval of BU Head, CRT Team accrues service credit, if any. This control ensures that a significant reversal in the amount of cumulative revenue recognized will not occur. 

ARC/ RRC is a variable consideration which will be measured monthly as whether the volume, amount, quantity of Operational services actually consumed or utilised under the relevant Process has gone above 15% of volume baseline. Hence estimation is not required and hence probability of revenue reversal will not occur.

Since producivity guarantee FTEs will be known at the end of each month, estimation of productivity is not required and hence there will be no significant reversal expected to occur.

section.name: Conclusion
section.instruction: Based on the answer to the question, determine if the contract exists between the parties

questions.question: Conclusion
questions.expected_answer:
Service Credit - Service credits should be recorded as reduction to revenue on monthly basis based on service level default & related percentages stated in the contract. Since the measurement period is monthly for some matrix, estimation of service credits at the inception and applying it monthly would give the same results. Hence, estimation can be foregone and service credit in total, cannot exceed the applicable At Risk Amount as per contract.
ARC/RRC  - The ARC and RRC fees rates would be applicable on the increased FTEs and decreased FTEs respectively. The ARC and RRC FTE rate would be used for recognition of the revenue on a monthly basis instead of the baseline FTE rate as contractually agreed, if applicable.
Productivity guarantee - The Productivity commitment is in the nature of efficiency gains which are being passed on to client over the period as mentioned in the current contract. This will be recorded as reduction of revenue in the form of reduction in monthly charges via lower headcount. The Company will do a monthly estimate of the efficiency benefits that will be passed on to the customer and any expected shortfall has to be recorded as a reduction to revenue over the measurement period. However, Estimation is not required since the productivity guarantee will be known at the end of each month.

step_section.name: C. Consideration payable to a customer:
step_section.instructions:
Guidance
Consideration payable to a customer includes cash amounts that an entity pays, or expects to pay, to the customer (or to other parties that purchase the Company’s goods or services from the customer) and credits or other items (e.g. coupon or voucher) that can be applied against amounts owed to the Company (or to other parties that purchase the Company’s goods or services from the customer).
